content.comment_body: Hello, I have a project with nine networked [product_name] modules and an HMI panel. The first [product_name] serves as the central unit, while the other eight connect and send signals to start and stop a pump. The challenge I'm facing is that there are too many network inputs for one [product_name] to manage. My question is whether it's possible to replace the central [product_name] with a [product_name] controller. The project needs 32 digital network inputs and 8 digital network outputs at the central station. Any guidance would be appreciated. Best regards, [user_name]
Is your issue the same as described in another topic about not having enough available connections? If so, what was the reason for creating a new thread?
Ah, I didn't remember that I had already posted about this earlier.

Thread closed because the question was asked in another post. The second thread with the subject 'No more connections available' was published in the [product_name] Communication section. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is encountering limitations with the maximum number of digital network inputs supported by a [product_name] module when used as the central controller. Their setup, which employs one module as a central hub for eight others, exceeds the device's networking capacity. This has led them to consider upgrading to a [product_name] controller for improved scalability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the central controller to reliably and efficiently manage at least 32 digital network inputs and 8 digital network outputs.
